unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the as-cast 3Cr steel strip (Table 1, wt.%): Mn 20.04, Al 9.09, C 1.23, Cr 3.09, S 0.0009, Fe Bal.
UTS × TE product for the as-cast 3Cr steel strip: 35.8 GPa % (Table 2).
Measured lattice parameter of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite in the as-cast 3Cr steel strip is 0.387 nm and 0.376 nm, respectively.
The ordered DO3 phase is a body centered cubic crystal with a lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm in the ferrite (Fe or Mn atoms at corner positions, Al or Fe/Mn atoms at every other centered positions).
The ideal stoichiometry of the κ-carbide is (Fe, Mn)3AlC, which has a perovskite crystal structure (Fe/Mn at corners, Al at face centers, C at the cube center).

A double (Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening behavior of the low-density steel strips: slip-band hardening acts at the early strain stage and microband hardening at the final strain stage; the number of nano-scale κ-carbides plays a crucial role in the strain hardening rate at the early strain stage.

For the as-cast 3Cr strip the κ-carbide volume fraction and average size are not explicitly reported; only that the volume fraction of κ-carbide decreases with Cr addition relative to the as-cast 0Cr strip (0Cr: 3%, 6 nm; annealed 0Cr: 7%, 8 nm; annealed 3Cr: 4%, 4 nm).
